bioParagraphs: I am a Software Engineering undergraduate at Pontifícia Universidade Católica de Minas Gerais (PUC Minas), passionate about the intersection between rigorous logic, systems architecture, and thoughtful interface design.

I believe building good software goes beyond writing functional code: it is about delivering pleasant, intuitive, and purpose-driven products. I cultivate a disciplined routine of continuous learning, diving deep into computer science fundamentals, object-oriented programming with Java, and the modern web ecosystem with JavaScript and React.

I operate natively with Artificial Intelligence, leveraging cutting-edge AI models and developer agents to explore novel ideas, rapidly prototype solutions, debug complex architectures, and sustain a productive engineering workflow, always applying critical judgment over code elegance and maintainability.

projects.degraueducaTagline: Web platform that organizes free courses into learning paths toward a first job
projects.degraueducaDesc: An interdisciplinary project at PUC Minas, built by a team of five. It gathers courses from recognized institutions into paths with a teaching order, saves each student's progress and includes an admin panel to manage the catalog. I handled the Design Thinking, the panel's CRUDs and part of sign-up and login.

degraueduca.docTitle: Degrau Educa, case study | Victor Cândido Leite
degraueduca.title: Degrau Educa
degraueduca.tagline: Climb each step of your career with purpose.
degraueduca.intro: A web platform that gathers free vocational courses from recognized institutions and organizes them into paths: courses in order, from the first one to a first job, with each student's progress saved.

meta.label: Context
meta.value: PUC Minas · Software Engineering · Interdisciplinary Project 1: Web Applications · 2026/1

meta.label: My role
meta.value: Design Thinking and UX, the admin panel with 4 CRUDs and part of sign-up and login

degraueduca.coverAlt: Degrau Educa home page: the headline "Climb each step of your career with purpose" and the buttons Explore Paths and See Courses

stats.label: collections in the JSON Server API

problem.title: Free courses are everywhere. Knowing which ones are worth it, and in what order, is not.
problem.body: Getting into the job market today takes more than a high school diploma. Platforms offer countless courses, and picking one, or planning a sequence of studies, becomes hard. With free courses it is worse: there is no way to tell which ones are good and recognized by employers.

quotes.label: What surprised us most
quotes.text: The rise in employability and average salary of people who take vocational courses, and the lack of tools that help place those courses on a résumé.

quotes.label: What mattered most
quotes.text: Studying online is widely accepted, and similar solutions exist that can serve as references.

quotes.label: Left to investigate
quotes.text: Which learning platforms and associations employers value most when choosing a candidate.

problem.note: Summary of the team's research highlights board.
problem.goal: Bring free courses from recognized platforms into one place, classify them by area of interest and chain them into paths with a logical, progressive sequence.

research.title: Before code, separate what we know from what we assume.
research.body: The process followed Design Thinking on Miro, from a template provided by the professors: a CSD Matrix to align certainties, assumptions and doubts, a stakeholder map, research, and personas with empathy maps and value propositions.

csd.label: Certainties
items: Institutions like SENAC, SESC, Udemy, Fundação Bradesco, USP and FGV offer free courses
These courses are not promoted in one central place

csd.label: Assumptions
items: Courses help people get into the job market
Tracking progress during a course makes a difference

csd.label: Doubts
items: How many students does the market actually hire?
What makes a student give up?
What age group looks for these courses?

research.csdAlt: CSD Alignment Matrix with the columns Doubts, Certainties and Assumptions
research.csdCaption: CSD Matrix: the doubts became research questions.
research.stakeholdersAlt: Stakeholder map in three circles: fundamental, important and influencers
research.stakeholdersCaption: Stakeholder map: students and learning platforms at the center; employers and the Ministry of Education at the edge.

personas.name: Lucas, 19
personas.role: Student looking for a first job
personas.want: Find free courses, improve his résumé and land a first job.
personas.pain: Too many options, no direction and low motivation: starts courses and drops them.
personas.design: Ready-made paths, plain language and encouragement along the way.

personas.name: Juliana, 32
personas.want: A promotion and new skills without leaving her job.
personas.pain: Lack of time, fatigue and trouble staying consistent.
personas.design: Focused courses, workload in plain sight and progress that picks up where she left off.

personas.name: Carlos, 28
personas.want: A job and practical skills to improve his life.
personas.pain: Phone-only access, limited internet and little familiarity with technology.
personas.design: A light, responsive, inclusive interface without jargon.

design.title: User stories, wireframes and a prototype before coding.
design.body: The personas became user stories in the "As a… I need… so that…" format and one value proposition each. From them came wireframes for five screens (home, login, profile, course and path), the user flow and a clickable prototype, used to validate navigation before writing code.
design.storiesAlt: User stories board with the columns As a, I need and So that
design.storiesCaption: User stories: each row links a persona to a need and its reason.
design.wireframeAlt: Hand-drawn wireframe of the path screen: courses in boxes linked by arrows, in a snake layout
design.wireframeCaption: Path wireframe: the snake layout was already on paper.
design.finalAlt: Implemented path screen: five courses in sequence, linked by dashed lines, each with a Completed switch
design.finalCaption: Implemented path: the same snake layout, with a completion switch on each course.
design.flowAlt: User flow with thumbnails of the home, login, user, path and courses screens
design.flowCaption: User flow: from the home screen to login, profile, paths and courses.

solution.title: One experience for those who study, another for those who run the catalog.
solution.body: Students browse the catalog, join paths, mark what they finished and follow their progress on the dashboard. All in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with Bootstrap and a REST API mocked by JSON Server. Pick a screen:

screens.title: Home page
screens.description: Main headline, shortcuts to paths and courses, and the featured paths.
screens.alt: Degrau Educa home page with the main headline and the start of the Our Paths section

screens.title: Course catalog
screens.description: Search by name or institution and filter by category. Each card shows workload and issuer.
screens.alt: Catalog with a search bar, category filters and course cards showing workload and issuer

screens.title: Course details
screens.description: Description, fact sheet and a link to the original platform. Logged in, students enroll and later mark it as completed.
screens.alt: Course page for Algorithms and Programming Logic with duration, issuer, description and fact sheet

screens.title: Path
screens.description: The path's courses in order, a completion switch on each, a progress bar and a heart to save it.
screens.alt: Introduction to Programming in Python path with five courses in a snake layout

screens.title: Student dashboard
screens.description: Consecutive login days, weekly goal, the current motivational message, course progress and a shortcut to resume the path.
screens.alt: Dashboard with a 5-day streak, a congratulations message, 100% progress and the Resume Path button

screens.title: Profile
screens.description: Personal data, area of interest, photo and the lists of courses in progress, completed and saved.
screens.alt: Profile with avatar, name, email, area of interest and lists of courses in progress, completed and saved

screens.title: Partners
screens.description: The 9 institutions behind the courses, with category and a link to each website.
screens.alt: Grid with partner logos such as Fundação Bradesco, Udemy, Senac and Curso em Vídeo

screens.title: Login and sign-up
screens.description: Username and password login; sign-up opens in a modal. Students go to the dashboard, admins to the panel.
screens.alt: Login screen with username and password fields and the Sign up link

admin.title: A panel to grow the catalog without touching code.
admin.body: Admins use the same login and land on a panel with four modules in the side menu. Each one is a CRUD over a JSON Server collection, using fetch with GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE, and an on-screen notice after every operation.

modules.title: Partners
modules.text: List, Create, Edit and Delete tabs. The list filters the table as you type; Edit suggests partners by name and fills the form; Delete removes several at once, with "select all".
modules.alt: Partners module: table with institution, category, link and logo, a search box and the Create, List, Edit and Delete tabs

modules.title: Courses
modules.text: One form creates and edits: title, workload, issuing partner, links, categories, summary, description, modules separated by semicolons and tags separated by commas. The slug comes from the title.
modules.alt: Edit form for the Algorithms and Programming Logic course with every field filled in

modules.title: Paths
modules.text: You check the path's courses and set the order students should take them in, with the ↑ and ↓ arrows. That order draws the snake layout on the student's screen.
modules.alt: Editing the Python path: checked courses and the Order of selected courses list with up and down arrows

modules.title: Motivational messages
modules.text: Encouraging messages fired by triggers: consecutive login days, total logins, finishing a course or a path, clicks and progress percentage.
modules.alt: Motivational Messages module with the event type and quantity form and the table of saved messages

code.title: Reordering a course in a path
code.text: Swaps the course with its neighbor and redraws the list; the arrows at the ends stay disabled.

code.title: Slug from the title
code.text: Strips accents and symbols to build the course address: "Lógica de Programação" becomes "logica-de-programacao".

code.title: Login that counts consecutive days
code.text: Every login adds to the total, but the streak only grows when the last visit was on another day. It feeds the dashboard and the messages.

admin.loginNote: In sign-up and login, I also worked on account creation (with password confirmation and a sequential id), the login that updates total visits and the day streak, and the redirect by profile: students to the dashboard, admins to the panel.

data.title: Seven collections and a mocked REST API.
data.body: No custom backend: JSON Server turns a JSON file into a REST API and serves the site's files. Collections link by id, and the logged-in user lives in localStorage.

collections.name: usuarios
collections.text: login, profile (user or admin), total logins and day streak

collections.name: cursos
collections.text: workload, issuer, reference link, modules, tags and categories

collections.name: jornadas
collections.text: ordered list of course ids, summary and categories

collections.name: progresso_usuario
collections.text: what each student saved, started or completed, with a date

collections.name: categorias
collections.text: Technology, Design and Creativity, Personal Development

collections.name: parceiros
collections.text: name, category, website and logo of each institution

data.exampleCaption: A path in db-educa.json: the course order is the array order.

stack.title: Plain web, from prototype to hosting.
stack.process: Planning was done together, with Scrum and Design Thinking. During development, each member took specific screens and CRUDs; merging the modules was done as a group again.

next.title: What I would do differently today.

items.title: Server-side authentication
items.text: Passwords are stored in plain text in the JSON file and login is checked in the browser. In a product, that moves to the server, with password hashing and sessions.

items.title: Feedback on the page
items.text: Replace alert() with messages next to the field that failed and ask for confirmation before deleting several records at once.

items.title: Tests for the CRUDs
items.text: Automated tests for the panel's operations, so merging the modules would not depend on checking everything by hand.

closing.title: Organizing the path is teaching too.
closing.text: Degrau Educa does not create courses: it picks the good ones and says in which order to take them. It was my first complete web project as part of a team, from personas to the panel that keeps it all running.
